Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** The relative link `[ws-doctor.spec.md](ws-doctor.spec.md)` in the Related list is broken in this registered plan copy: it resolves to `.agents/plans/enable-auditing/ws-doctor.spec.md`, which does not exist (the directory contains only this file). The identical link works in the spec of record at `.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md` because `.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md` exists — the link was copied verbatim into a different directory without adjusting the relative target. Anyone following the reference from the plan artifact lands on a 404.

**Correção sugerida:**

```diff
-- Related: [`ws-doctor.spec.md`](ws-doctor.spec.md) (static diagnose), `ws-check-harness`, `ws-fable-judge`, `ws-multi-spec`, `ws-github-provider` (issue creation via `gh` when user accepts).
+- Related: [`ws-doctor.spec.md`](../specs/ws-doctor.spec.md) (static diagnose), `ws-check-harness`, `ws-fable-judge`, `ws-multi-spec`, `ws-github-provider` (issue creation via `gh` when user accepts).
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 3/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: directory listing of `.agents/plans/enable-auditing/` shows only `step-00-enable-auditing.spec.md`; `ws-doctor.spec.md` exists only at `.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md`. The spec file line 90 contains `Related: [ws-doctor.spec.md](ws-doctor.spec.md)`. 2. Scenario: a maintainer opening the registered plan copy clicks the link to review the related static-diagnose spec and gets a missing-file 404. 3. Protection: the plan/spec artifacts are not covered by the ws-doctor link checker (it scans skills root and hubs only, not `{plansDir}`), so no automated gate catches it. 4. Discards: considered whether the link is intended as a bare filename reference — the markdown syntax makes it a navigable link, and the sibling file in the same PR (`.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md`) resolves, so the discrepancy is real.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/plans/enable-auditing/step-00-enable-auditing.spec.md, /.agents/specs/enable-auditing.spec.md, /.agents/specs/ws-doctor.spec.md
</details>

<!-- resolution-reply -->

Fixed: plan copy Related link now points to ../specs/ws-doctor.spec.md (commit 423bdd0).

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** This boundary table links a Workflows-package skill to an Extra-package skill via a real relative path. `ws-doctor` ships in the Workflows package (`bin/skill-dependencies.json` `packages.workflows.skills`), while `ws-show-harness` ships only in the Extra package (`packages.extra.skills`). In a Workflows-only install (the default `--package workflows`), `ws-show-harness` is absent, so `../ws-show-harness/SKILL.md` is a broken link in the shipped body — and, ironically, the doctor's own path scan will then report its own SKILL.md as a missing reference on the very surface it is meant to keep clean. The repository explicitly isolates Extra skills to avoid phantom routes in Workflows-only installs (root AGENTS.md scope note; ws-shared/AGENTS.md `### Extra package (optional)`), and no other Workflows skill links to an Extra skill (ws-check-harness and ws-check-workflows do not).

**Correção sugerida:**

```markdown
| Skill | Use when |
|-------|----------|
| **This skill** | Broken paths after token expand, missing launchers / scripts, parse failures, live `config.json` summary, missing companion refs |
| [`ws-check-harness`](../ws-check-harness/SKILL.md) | Phases 0-5c integrity, routing, portability, digests, topology |
| `ws-show-harness` (Extra package) | What is active in the **current session** |
```
(Keep the boundary note but drop the relative link so Workflows-only installs have no phantom path.)

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 6/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: bin/skill-dependencies.json lines 25-66 put ws-doctor in workflows and lines 72-75 put ws-show-harness in extra; root AGENTS.md scope note states Extra skills are 'absent from Workflows-only installs' and that consumer routes keep them isolated 'so Workflows-only installs avoid phantom routes'; grep across `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` shows only ws-doctor references ws-show-harness (line 28); ws-check-harness and ws-check-workflows bodies contain no Extra-skill links. 2. Scenario: consumer installs `--package workflows`; `ws-show-harness` is not copied; doctor scans its own SKILL.md, resolves `../ws-show-harness/SKILL.md` against `.agents/skills/ws-doctor/`, finds nothing, and emits a false path-error finding for its own body. 3. Protection: `ws-check-harness` runs in this repo where ws-show-harness exists on disk, so the link resolves and no phase flags it; the workflows-only install layout is never audited. 4. Discards: the row is prose (a 'use when' boundary note) and could be considered non-routing — but it is a literal file path in the shipped body, which is exactly the phantom-path class the harness avoids; moving the mention to ws-shared/AGENTS.md Extra section would preserve the note without the broken link.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-doctor/SKILL.md, /bin/skill-dependencies.json, /.agents/skills/ws-shared/AGENTS.md, /.agents/skills/ws-check-harness/SKILL.md
</details>

Agentic Code Reviewer opencode

💡 **SUGGESTION:** The template-detection predicate tests the same condition twice: `t.includes('\u2026')` appears as both the second and third clause. The adjacent `asciiSafe` helper (line 129) shows the author distinguishes `'...'` (three ASCII dots) from the single ellipsis character `\u2026`, so the duplicated clause likely hid a third intended variant (for example the two-dot leader `\u2025` or midline ellipsis `\u22EF`). The redundancy has no runtime impact today, but it masks the lost clause and invites a future fix in the wrong place.

**Correção sugerida:**

```js
if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026') || t.includes('\u2025') || t.includes('\u22EF')) return true;
// Or, if no extra variant is intended, simply drop the duplicate:
// if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026')) return true;
```

<details>
<summary>🔍 Detalhes da Análise IA</summary>

**Score:** 3/10 | **Ação dev:** fix-code

**Análise:**
1. Evidence: doctor.js line 226 reads `if (t.includes('...') || t.includes('\u2026') || t.includes('\u2026')) return true;` — third clause identical to second; asciiSafe line 129 maps `\u2026` to '...' separately from the ASCII '...' case. 2. Scenario: no functional failure — the duplicate is idempotent; the risk is a missed ellipsis-like variant because the intended clause was overwritten by copy-paste. 3. Protection: all smoke tests pass regardless, so nothing guards the predicate's completeness. 4. Discards: it is not a crash or misclassification (the condition still returns true for ellipsis-containing strings), so severity is minimal; it is still a provable defect in new code rather than style preference.

**Caminhos analisados:** /.agents/skills/ws-doctor/scripts/doctor.js
</details>
